summary: RETEST of iteration_94's regression fix on RadarView.tsx (removal of `.requireExternalGestureToFail(pinch)` from the Pan gesture, keeping pinchActive early-return guards + pinch never touching Follow Mode). Tested via browser Preview (mobile viewport 375x667) using kauri@intro.demo (token via localStorage, already visible=true). REGRESSION IS FIXED: single-finger pan/drag now correctly activates the Pan gesture (verified via mouse down/move/up simulation with 15-20 intermediate move events) -- Follow Mode reliably turns OFF (locate icon rgb(156,163,175) grey) the moment a real drag exceeds minDistance(12), confirmed both at default zoom (scale=1) and after zooming in. When zoomed in (scale>1, so pan bounds are non-zero), the world-layer transform visibly translates during the drag (e.g. translateX(-56px) translateY(-32px)) and the 'You' marker moves with it -- confirmed via direct inline-style inspection, not just screenshots. At scale=1 the pan gesture still correctly fires onStart/disables Follow Mode, but there is zero visible translation because boundX/boundY = ((scale-1)*MAP_W)/2 evaluates to exactly 0 at scale=1 -- this is a mathematical consequence of the existing bound-clamping formula (not a new bug), so 'moving freely' is only observable once zoomed in past 1x, matching how the zoom-button/pan interaction is designed to compose. Recentre button after a manual pan (while zoomed in) smoothly springs tx/ty back toward 0 and scale back toward 1, and the locate icon returns to teal -- confirmed programmatically (transform read back near 0,0 and scale converging to 1 mid-spring, colour teal). Zoom +/- buttons work correctly while Follow Mode is off and the viewport is off-centre: pan translation (tx=-56,ty=-32) stayed fixed through 2 zoom-in/zoom-out button presses while only scale changed (2.99 -> 3.0 -> 1.85), Follow Mode stayed grey throughout, no crash, no forced re-centre. Regression-of-regression fully re-confirmed: on a fresh Follow-Mode-ON load, zoom-in x4, zoom-out x4, double-tap-in and double-tap-out all left the 'You' marker at the exact same pixel position (179,308) with the locate icon staying teal rgb(32,178,170) throughout -- zero drift, exactly matching iteration_94's earlier passing result, confirming removing requireExternalGestureToFail introduced no new breakage here. General regression: rings, clusters, business/event pins, radius discovery sheet (opens correctly listing 100m/250m/500m/750m/1km options), Filters, Events chip all render with no console errors or crashes. Genuine 2-finger pinch simulation was not attempted this session (browser/CDP multi-touch simulation is unreliable/not verified in this environment per prior sessions) -- stating this explicitly as a known Preview limitation requiring a real device/native build for full pinch confidence, per the task's own guidance, rather than guessing pass/fail.

issues: Not a regression, just a UX note: single-finger pan disables Follow Mode correctly at any zoom level, but produces zero visible map movement while scale==1 (default zoom) because boundX/boundY = ((scale-1)*MAP_W)/2 clamp to exactly 0 at 1x. Users dragging at default zoom will see the locate button turn grey but the map/You marker won't visibly move until they've also zoomed in at least slightly. Consider whether this matches intended UX (e.g. maybe pan should be allowed a small fixed exploration radius even at scale=1) -- flagging for product/design confirmation, not blocking.

When zoomed in, the map/You marker visibly translate during drag (confirmed via inline transform inspection, e.g. translateX(-56px) translateY(-32px))

Zoom +/- buttons work correctly while Follow Mode is off / viewport off-centre: tx/ty stay fixed, only scale changes, no forced re-centre, no crash, colour stays grey

Regression-of-regression confirmed: zoom-in x4, zoom-out x4, double-tap-in, double-tap-out with Follow Mode ON all keep 'You' marker at pixel-exact position (179,308) with locate icon staying teal -- zero drift, no new breakage from removing requireExternalGestureToFail
No crashes/red-screens/console errors across all tested states; rings, clusters, event/business pins, radius discovery sheet, filters chip, events chip all render correctly

critical_code_review_comments: Confirmed via direct source review that `.requireExternalGestureToFail(pinch)` has been removed from the Pan gesture chain (RadarView.tsx line ~318-354); pan is now `Gesture.Pan().minDistance(12).maxPointers(1)` with only the pinchActive early-return guards remaining in onStart/onUpdate/onEnd, exactly as described.

pinch.onStart/onUpdate/onEnd still correctly never touch followSV/setFollowMode, and pan.onStart/onUpdate/onEnd still correctly early-return whenever pinchActive.value is true -- both intended safety nets intact.

The zero-visible-pan-at-scale=1 behaviour stems from `boundX = ((scale.value - 1) * MAP_W) / 2` / same for boundY inside pan.onUpdate -- this is pre-existing logic, not something this session's fix touched, and is mathematically correct for a clamp-to-current-zoom-extent pan model; just calling it out since it affects how 'freely moving' looks to a tester/user at 1x zoom.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The iteration_94 regression is CONFIRMED FIXED. Key technique used to verify pan actually moves the map (not just toggles Follow Mode): read the inline `style` attribute directly off the worldLayer Reanimated.View (first element under [data-testid='radar-map'] matching `[style*='translate']`) via page.evaluate + querySelectorAll, rather than relying on screenshot pixel-diffing (screenshots can look visually identical even when transform values changed by small px amounts, and at scale=1 they genuinely don't change at all since pan bounds clamp to 0 there -- zoom in first via radar-zoom-in x3 before testing pan if you want to see visible movement). To read the locate button colour reliably use `getComputedStyle` on the Ionicons DOM node inside [data-testid='radar-recentre'], not the button element itself. 2-finger pinch was still not simulated -- if a future task specifically needs pinch confidence, real-device/native testing is required since CDP multi-touch has been unreliable across sessions.
rca_of_issue: N/A this session -- fix verified working, no new RCA needed. For historical reference: iteration_94's regression was caused by `.requireExternalGestureToFail(pinch)` deadlocking Pan because Pinch (minPointers=2 by default) never reliably signalled FAILED during a live single-finger touch in the web/CDP gesture-handler runtime. Removing that call (this iteration's fix) and relying solely on the pinchActive shared-value early-return guards resolved it completely with no observed side effects.
